title: GraphFI: An Efficient Fault Injection Framework for Graph Processing on GPGPUs
problem: Existing fault injection methods ignore graph-specific execution paradigms (iterations, vertices, error propagation), producing inaccurate system error resilience characterization and blind fault injection trials that are computationally expensive.
motivation: Graph processing is increasingly deployed in safety-critical domains (financial fraud detection, power systems), requiring reliable execution beyond raw performance, but traditional FI frameworks waste effort on non-representative errors.
method: GraphFI avoids testing billions of possible fault scenarios by finding patterns in how graphs execute on GPUs. It selects representative moments in execution when similar vertices are computing (iteration-driven), groups vertices by how similarly they fail when faults occur (topology-driven), and uses fault monotonicity—the principle that worse faults always produce worse outcomes—to predict which failures would be severe without testing all possibilities. Combining these three strategies cuts the test scenarios needed by up to 100x.
key_novelty: GraphFI is the first fault-injection framework to use graph-specific execution patterns—iteration phases, vertex grouping, and fault monotonicity—to reduce testing trials by 2.1–15.2x while improving reliability assessment.
contributions: Iteration-driven GraphFI selecting representative iterations based on active vertex similarity.
Topology-driven GraphFI identifying resilience-similarity communities in graph topology.
Monotonicity-driven GraphFI leveraging fault monotonic property to predict error boundaries and avoid unnecessary injection.

metrics.other: up to 100x reduction in fault site space

primary_theme: graph-specific fault injection for GPU reliability
